title: Monitoring & Logging
description: Set up health checks, structured logging, and metrics for observability.

slides.title: Health Checks 🏥
slides.content:
# Keep Your API Alive

Add a health check endpoint that can be used by load balancers and orchestration systems.

```python
@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    # Check database, cache, etc.
    return {"status": "ok"}
```

Return 200 if healthy, else 500 with details.

slides.title: Structured Logging
slides.content:
Use JSON logs for easier parsing by log aggregation tools (e.g., ELK, Datadog).

```python
import structlog

logger = structlog.get_logger()

@app.get("/")
async def root():
    logger.info("Root endpoint called", extra={"user": "anonymous"})
    return {"message": "Hello"}
```

Configure structlog to output JSON in production.
slides.codeSnippet:
import structlog

structlog.configure(
    processors=[
        structlog.processors.JSONRenderer()
    ]
)

logger = structlog.get_logger()

logger.info("App started", version="1.0.0")

slides.title: Metrics with Prometheus
slides.content:
# Monitor Performance

Use `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator` to expose metrics.

```bash
pip install prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator
```

```python
from prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator import Instrumentator

instrumentator = Instrumentator().instrument(app).expose(app)
```

Now metrics are available at `/metrics` for Prometheus to scrape.

slides.title: Basic Monitoring Setup
slides.content:
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator import Instrumentator

app = FastAPI()

instrumentator = Instrumentator().instrument(app)

@app.on_event("startup")
async def startup():
    instrumentator.expose(app)

@app.get("/")
async def root():
    return {"message": "Hello"}
```

Now you can see request count, latency, etc., at `/metrics`.
slides.codeSnippet:
from prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator import Instrumentator

app = FastAPI()
Instrumentator().instrument(app).expose(app)

# After this, /metrics endpoint is available.
